title: Types and Categories of Ration Cards

facts.summary: Ration-card categories are used within the Public Distribution System to identify households eligible for different types of food-grain benefits. The applicable categories and implementation are determined under the relevant national framework and by State or Union Territory authorities.
facts.priority_household: Priority Households (PHH) are households identified as eligible under the National Food Security Act according to the applicable State or Union Territory identification criteria.
facts.antyodaya_anna_yojana: Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) covers households identified under the applicable AAY criteria for food-grain entitlements under the NFSA framework.
facts.state_specific_categories: States and Union Territories may use their own terminology, classifications, or administrative categories in addition to the categories used under the applicable national framework.
facts.eligibility: Eligibility and identification of households for applicable ration-card categories are handled by the concerned State or Union Territory according to the applicable rules and criteria.
facts.benefits: The food-grain entitlement associated with a household depends on the applicable category and prevailing government rules.
important_notes: PHH and AAY are important beneficiary categories under the NFSA framework.
The State or Union Territory is responsible for identifying eligible households.
Ration-card terminology and administrative classifications can vary between States and Union Territories.
Do not assume that every State or Union Territory uses exactly the same ration-card categories or terminology.
Eligibility for a particular category should be confirmed with the concerned State/UT authority.

faqs.question: What are the types of ration cards?
faqs.answer: Under the NFSA framework, important beneficiary categories include Priority Household (PHH) and Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY). State and Union Territory classifications may vary.

faqs.question: What is a PHH ration card?
faqs.answer: PHH refers to a Priority Household identified as eligible under the NFSA framework according to the applicable State or Union Territory criteria.

faqs.question: What is an AAY ration card?
faqs.answer: AAY refers to Antyodaya Anna Yojana, a category covering households identified under the applicable AAY criteria for food-grain entitlements.

faqs.question: What is the difference between PHH and AAY?
faqs.answer: PHH and AAY are different beneficiary categories under the NFSA framework. Their eligibility and applicable entitlements are governed by the relevant rules and identification criteria.

faqs.question: Who decides which ration-card category I belong to?
faqs.answer: The concerned State or Union Territory identifies eligible households according to the applicable criteria.

faqs.question: Are ration-card categories the same in every State?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. States and Union Territories may use different administrative classifications or terminology. The applicable State/UT authority should be consulted.

faqs.question: How do I know my ration-card category?
faqs.answer: Check your ration-card records or the official ration-card system of the concerned State or Union Territory.
